opening.text: A gardener has a small bag of seed. He could eat it. Or he could plant it. The first seeds go into the ground before anything else. Then he waits. It takes faith to plant seed you could have used today. Tithing is like that first planting. We give the first portion, and we trust that God will grow something good.

mainMessage.text: Tithing is the first seed we plant. God grows what we give Him.

blocks.text: **A gift we get to give** Tithing is not a bill. It is a chance to put God first.
Honour the Lord with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.
Elder Ronald E. Poelman of the Seventy said this in his talk “Tithing: A Privilege” from the April 1998 general conference.
You and I are now among those generations given the privilege to know and to live the law of the tithe.
It is a privilege.
**Light through the window** Malachi spoke of the windows of heaven. Windows let light in. Tithing opens a way for the Lord's light to come into our lives.

Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Windows of Heaven” from the October 2013 general conference.
Windows allow natural light to enter into a building.
The window lets in light.
**He keeps His word** The Lord has made a promise about tithing. He does not forget it.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Tithing: Opening the Windows of Heaven” from the October 2023 general conference.
I promise you that as you trust in the Lord, the blessings of heaven will follow.
The promise is real.
**Blessings of many kinds** The blessings may be money, health or peace. Often they are things we can't count. They come in more ways than one.

Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Windows of Heaven” from the October 2013 general conference.
I testify spiritual and temporal blessings come into our lives as we live the law of tithing.
The blessings come in many ways.
**Where our hearts are** Jesus said our hearts follow our treasure. Tithing helps point our hearts toward Him.

Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Windows of Heaven” from the October 2013 general conference.
The honest payment of tithing is much more than a duty; it is an important step in the process of personal sanctification.
It shapes the heart.
**Trust is the power** Tithing asks us to trust, even when the numbers look tight. Trust is where the power starts.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Tithing: Opening the Windows of Heaven” from the October 2023 general conference.
The power comes from placing our trust in the Lord.
Start with trust.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they paid tithing and saw a blessing, even a small one. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The widow and the prophet

blocks.text: A widow was down to her last bit of flour and oil. The prophet Elijah asked her to feed him first.

And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son. For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.
She gave first, and she had enough. God honored her faith, one day at a time.

application.text: First, set aside the first tenth when you get paid. Second, say a short prayer of thanks as you do. Third, notice what you are given in return.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know tithing is a gift to God. I know He keeps His promises. I know Jesus Christ is the giver of every good thing. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

versions.analogy: The first seed in the garden
invitations: I invite you to set aside the first tenth when you get paid.
I invite you to say a short prayer of thanks as you do.
I invite you to notice what you are given in return.
blessings: You will receive the blessings the Lord has promised.
You will see His hand in your life.

closingVerse.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

opening.text: In a small village, one well served every family. Everyone drew from it. And everyone helped keep it clean and deep. If some families stopped helping, the well suffered. If all pitched in, no one went thirsty. Tithing is like that well. It's a shared gift. And it blesses each person who gives.

mainMessage.text: Tithing fills a well for all of us. When we give, we receive too.

blocks.text: **Honoring the well** We give the first and best of what we have. That says we put God first.
Honour the Lord with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.
Elder Ronald E. Poelman of the Seventy said this in his talk “Tithing: A Privilege” from the April 1998 general conference.
You and I are now among those generations given the privilege to know and to live the law of the tithe.
We are given the privilege.
**Let the light in** The windows of heaven let in light. When we give, the Lord lets His light in.

Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Windows of Heaven” from the October 2013 general conference.
Windows allow natural light to enter into a building.
The light comes in.
**A promise at the well** The Lord has promised to bless those who trust Him. He will do what He said.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Tithing: Opening the Windows of Heaven” from the October 2023 general conference.
I promise you that as you trust in the Lord, the blessings of heaven will follow.
He will follow through.
**The water comes in more than one way** Some blessings are plain, like having enough. Others are quiet, like peace of mind. Both are real.

Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Windows of Heaven” from the October 2013 general conference.
I testify spiritual and temporal blessings come into our lives as we live the law of tithing.
Both kinds are real.
**A well-kept heart** The well keeps the village alive. Tithing keeps our hearts close to God.

Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Windows of Heaven” from the October 2013 general conference.
The honest payment of tithing is much more than a duty; it is an important step in the process of personal sanctification.
It makes us better.
**Trust the well** No one doubts the well will have water. We can trust the Lord in the same way.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Tithing: Opening the Windows of Heaven” from the October 2023 general conference.
The power comes from placing our trust in the Lord.
Trust the source.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they gave to something bigger than themselves. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Abram gives tithes

blocks.text: After a hard battle, Abram met a priest named Melchizedek. Abram gave him a tenth of all he had.

And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God. And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth: And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all.
Abram knew where his victory came from. He gave back out of gratitude. Tithing began as thanks.

application.text: First, write down three things you are grateful for. Second, pay your tithing as a way to say thank you. Third, thank God out loud when you do.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know tithing is a way to say thank you to God. I know the blessings come. I know Jesus Christ gave us everything. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to write down three things you are grateful for.
I invite you to pay your tithing as a way to say thank you.

You will feel closer to God.
You will see how much you have been given.

closingVerse.text: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.

blocks.text: **Setting the barrel** We set aside the first tenth. It shows that God comes first.

I promise you that as you trust in the Lord, the blessings of heaven will follow.

Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

Many needs are served.

Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Windows of Heaven” from the October 2013 general conference.

Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Tithing: Opening the Windows of Heaven” from the October 2023 general conference.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they gave a little and felt that it mattered. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The widow's two mites

blocks.text: Jesus sat near the temple treasury and watched people give. Many rich people gave a lot. Then a poor widow came.

And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much. And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing. And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.
Jesus saw her heart. He looks at faith, not the size of the gift. Tithing is the same: a tenth of little is still a full gift.

application.text: First, pay your tithing before spending on other things this month. Second, don't compare your amount to anyone else's. Third, thank the Lord for whatever you have.

invitations: I invite you to pay your tithing before spending on other things this month.

Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a small offering turned out to be enough. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The boy's lunch

blocks.text: A huge crowd had gathered, and everyone was hungry. A boy had five small loaves and two small fish.

There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many? And Jesus said, Make the men sit down. Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand. And Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to them that were set down; and likewise of the fishes as much as they would.
The boy's lunch was small. In the Savior's hands it was enough for thousands. What we offer, even when small, can become more in His hands.

closingVerse.text: He who receiveth all things with thankfulness shall be made glorious; and the things of this earth shall be added unto him, even an hundred fold, yea, more.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they trusted God with their money, even when it was hard. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jacob's promise at Bethel

blocks.text: Jacob was running from home and sleeping on a stone. He had nothing. He made a promise to God.

And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father’s house in peace; then shall the Lord be my God: And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God’s house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.
Jacob promised a tenth when he had almost nothing. He trusted God before he had anything to show for it. That is faith.

application.text: First, think about where trust is hard for you. Second, tell the Lord about it in prayer. Third, take one faithful step, such as paying tithing first, and see what He does.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

invitations: I invite you to think about where trust is hard for you.
I invite you to tell the Lord about it in prayer.

blessings: Your trust in Him will deepen.
The Lord will hear your prayer.
You will see His blessings in His time.

closingVerse.text: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid; for the Lord Jehovah is my strength and my song; he also has become my salvation.
